text.p: Sypertyphoon Dale is currently over open water in the western Pacific Ocean near 18n/132e, moving northwest at 9 mph. Dale has top winds of 160 mph and is expected to very gradually weaken. Dale is expected to begin a turn to the north and will probably pass about 150-200 miles east of Okinawa, Japan, early Wednesday. Dale will be a major threat to shipping. It will also stir up very rough surf and high waves which will batter southeastern Japan, the southern Japanese islands, and as far west as eastern Taiwan and the eastern coast of mainland China.

Tropical Storm Ernie is expected to have 45-50 mph winds during the next 24-36 hours. During this time, the storm will become nearly stationary in the South China Sea, southeast of Hong Kong near 21n/117e, threatening only shipping. It will be watched for possible landfall in a few days in southern China.

Tropical Cyclone Melanie-Bellamine is now dissipating in the Indian Ocean near 22s/77e. The storm is moving southwest and will turn to the south, dissipating in about 48 hours. Top winds are 45 mph, but will continue to weaken. The threat to shipping will gradually diminish.
THERE ARE NO FURTHER EMERGENCY WEATHER STATEMENTS
